match.reason: The bank point e-rational covers rational decision making in general, while the new point specifically teaches marginal thinking, comparing the extra benefit of one more unit with its extra cost, which e-rational does not teach.

draft.title: Marginal thinking
card: Marginal means extra. Marginal benefit is the extra benefit from one more unit. Marginal cost is the extra cost of one more unit.
A rational decision compares the two. If the marginal benefit is greater than the marginal cost, doing one more unit makes the decision-maker better off.
If the marginal cost is greater than the marginal benefit, one more unit makes them worse off, so they should not do it.
A rational decision-maker keeps going while marginal benefit is higher than marginal cost, and stops where the two meet. Marginal benefit often falls as more units are used.
draft.remember: Do one more unit while its extra benefit beats its extra cost. Stop where they meet.

a.q: Leila is deciding how many hours to study for a test. What does a rational decision about the next hour compare?
opts: The extra benefit of that hour with its extra cost
The total hours studied so far with the hours left
The cost of the first hour with the cost of the last
The benefit of all her study with the benefit of none
a.why: Marginal thinking looks at the one extra hour, comparing the extra benefit it brings with the extra cost it carries. Comparing totals or earlier hours does not tell her whether one more hour is worth it.
a.clue: Look at the next unit only, not the whole amount.

b.q: Sam runs a food truck in Geelong. Opening for one more hour tonight would cost him $60 in wages and fuel, and he expects it to bring in $40 of extra benefit. What should a rational Sam do?
opts: Close, because the extra cost is more than the extra benefit
Open, because he has already spent money on the truck today
Open, because the extra hour would still earn some benefit
Close, because the first hours tonight earned less than $60
b.why: The extra hour costs $60 and brings only $40, so marginal cost is greater than marginal benefit and he would be worse off. Some benefit is not enough: the extra benefit has to be at least as large as the extra cost.
b.clue: Compare the extra $ the hour brings with the extra $ it costs.

a.best: The extra benefit of that hour with its extra cost

b.best: Close, because the extra cost is more than the extra benefit
